setting: The story is set at a university in present-day Seoul. Everyday life revolves around first crushes, club activities, coursework and the 24-hour convenience store. The distance Korea's senior-junior hierarchy puts between the player and the members, and the shy testing of new feelings, are where the whole story's tension lives.

statNotes.selfId: Rises when she says what she actually wants in a room where an answer is expected - a seminar, a club meeting, a group project. Falls when she gives the answer that keeps things smooth.
statNotes.secrecy: Falls when the relationship becomes legible to anyone on campus - a classmate in the same seminar, a club group chat, a photo someone else posted, being seen leaving together late. Rises when an ordinary explanation holds.
statNotes.mood: Driven by deadlines, exams and where the semester is, and by how the last conversation with the target member ended.

identities.name: Café owner
identities.background: [Identity: Café owner] You own the café at {name}'s university, and the members come in all the time - for coffee, to study, for group projects, to hang out. Typical events: They stop by for coffee in the morning, and you quietly memorise {name}'s order; At the weekend they meet at the café for a game night, and {name} asks you to join in; Chatting with {name} while she orders, you learn a little more about her life. Advantage: You have natural, everyday contact with them. Disadvantage: You can only ever wait at the café for her to come in, with no reason of your own to go and see her. [First meeting] The story opens on the first time the two of you meet: before round 1, you and {name} have never really met - a name you had heard, a face you had passed. So this relationship starts from nothing: round 1 is written with the distance and the testing of a first meeting, and affection grows a little with every round after it.

identities.name: Classmate
identities.background: [Identity: Classmate] You are in the same year and the same department as {name} and the others, and you got to know each other naturally when you started. Typical events: Assigned to the same group project, you drink coffee together and stay up all night to finish it; She falls asleep in the seat beside you in class and her head tips slowly toward your shoulder; On the day exams end the whole department is celebrating and the two of you leave early. Advantage: The shortest distance and the most reasons to see each other. Disadvantage: And for exactly that reason, the line between love and friendship blurs. [First meeting] The story opens on the first time the two of you meet: before round 1, you and {name} have never really met - a name you had heard, a face you had passed. So this relationship starts from nothing: round 1 is written with the distance and the testing of a first meeting, and affection grows a little with every round after it.

identities.name: Senior
identities.background: [Identity: Senior] You are the members' mentor senior, a year above them in the same department, and you got to know them naturally when they started as first-years. Typical events: The members arrive as first-years and you are the one sent to show them around; She brings her course list to ask you which classes are worth taking; A club dinner ends and you walk her back to the dorms; The first time she presents her hands shake, and you are the one who encourages her. Advantage: A built-in reason to spend time together, and being her senior makes looking after her look obvious. Disadvantage: For exactly that reason, being her senior makes any step across the line a careful one. [First meeting] The story opens on the first time the two of you meet: before round 1, you and {name} have never really met - a name you had heard, a face you had passed. So this relationship starts from nothing: round 1 is written with the distance and the testing of a first meeting, and affection grows a little with every round after it.

identities.name: Junior
identities.background: [Identity: Junior] You are a year below the members and got to know them naturally when you started; she is the first senior in the department whose name you learned. Typical events: She gives you her notes and holds nothing back; In the club she takes on the errand that was about to be pushed onto you; At a dinner someone keeps refilling your glass and she takes it away; You are up all night on an assignment and she stays in the study room until you finish. Advantage: Asking a senior for help is the most natural way to get close. Disadvantage: For exactly that reason, being her junior makes any step across the line a careful one. [First meeting] The story opens on the first time the two of you meet: before round 1, you and {name} have never really met - a name you had heard, a face you had passed. identities.name: Teaching assistant
identities.background: [Identity: Teaching Assistant] You are the TA for a new course the members are taking this semester: you guide their course projects, hold office hours and mark their work, and you get to know them naturally through the course. Typical events: You write a note in the margin of her report that is longer than an ordinary comment; Office hours empty out until it is just the two of you, and the subject left the course a while ago; She hands an assignment in at the last possible minute and you do not ask; Marking a pile of work, you recognise her handwriting at a glance. Advantage: The position is ambiguous - you have a little authority and can help her, which makes getting close easy. Disadvantage: The rule that a TA stays fair and plays no favourites. [First meeting] The story opens on the first time the two of you meet: before round 1, you and {name} have never really met - a name you had heard, a face you had passed. So this relationship starts from nothing: round 1 is written with the distance and the testing of a first meeting, and affection grows a little with every round after it.

identities.name: Exchange student
identities.background: [Identity: Exchange Student] You have just arrived at the university on a one-semester exchange, in the same year and department as the members, and you are not yet at home in Korean or in Korea. Typical events: In a group discussion you cannot keep up with the speed, so she slows down and helps translate for you; She takes you to the place only local students know about; You say a word wrong, she laughs for a long time, and then teaches you the right way to say it; You get as far as when you are leaving and you both change the subject. Advantage: Being an exchange student keeps attention on the two of you low and the pressure of gossip light. Disadvantage: Everyone knows you are leaving, her included - it has been a premise you both share since the first day. [First meeting] The story opens on the first time the two of you meet: before round 1, you and {name} have never really met - a name you had heard, a face you had passed. So this relationship starts from nothing: round 1 is written with the distance and the testing of a first meeting, and affection grows a little with every round after it.

modes.free: [Story Mode: Free] No authored plot events - the relationship itself is the plot. Affection grows slowly. Focus on details and subtle tension: the same seats, the same walk back, a semester passing. No rushing into relationship.
modes.romance: [Story Mode: Romance] Ambiguous & Romantic. Natural progression with mutual attraction. Members flirt during Flirting stage.
modes.pressure: [Story Mode: Pressure] Department gossip and social visibility higher, secrecy changes doubled. Being seen together carries weight: a classmate's photo, a club group chat, a name that travels faster than the syllabus.
modes.dramatic: [Story Mode: Dramatic] Light comedic. Love triangle scenes probability doubled. Members compete more openly for your attention.

phases.start: Shared classes and corridors, polite distance, subtle curiosity. No romantic moves.
phases.develop: Growing familiarity, late-night study rooms, accidental touches, first hints of jealousy.
phases.climax: Department talk, a photo someone else posted, family expectations, plans after graduation against feelings.
phases.resolve: Exposure risk, possible proposal or separation.
